shower.thought: We spend our whole lives trying to be ourselves, but we only ever become more like the people we've known.
The worst part of getting older isn't losing abilities—it's realizing which ones you'll actually never use again.
You can't remember most of your life, so statistically you're already mostly dead and just don't know it yet.
Money is just proof that you did something someone else found valuable enough to trade their time for.
Everyone thinks they're the main character in the story, which means most conversations are two monologues passing each other.
You're nostalgic for times when you weren't actually happy—you're nostalgic for being younger while experiencing them.
The only people who truly understand your childhood are people you'll probably never talk to again.
Your phone knows more about what you actually want than you do, which is why its suggestions feel invasive.
We call it "falling asleep" but really consciousness is just losing its grip on you.
The reason you can't tickle yourself is the same reason you can't surprise yourself—your brain is too busy predicting you.
Most of what you believe about yourself comes from things other people said about you once.
You'll probably spend more time thinking about people you dislike than people you love, but call it wasted time.
The internet didn't make people meaner—it just gave meanness an audience.
Every photo you take is you trying to convince your future self that you were happy here.
You can't be lonely and bored at the same time, which is why loneliness feels worse than emptiness.
The saddest part of growing up is realizing your parents were just figuring it out too.
Time moves slower when you're not sure what you're waiting for.
You never actually know if you're doing something because you want to or because you're afraid of what happens if you don't.
Regret is just wishing you had different information, not a different self.
Forgiveness is possible because everyone's already forgotten what they did wrong anyway.

darkjoke.thought:
I went to a self-help seminar titled "Find Your Purpose."
Turns out my purpose was just to pay for the seminar.

My dad said, "Son, I'm very disappointed in you."
I said, "Join the club." He said, "There's a club?" I said, "Yeah, it meets every Sunday. It's called my family."

I asked my friend why he never goes to the gym anymore.
He said, "I realized I'm just paying money to be disappointed in myself in a different location."

My therapist asked what my biggest fear was.
I said, "That one day I'll realize I've been the problem the whole time." She said, "That's called progress." I said, "That's called a panic attack."

I told my girlfriend she was being paranoid about me cheating.
She said, "Am I?" I said, "Well, you are now."

My doctor said, "You need to cut back on drinking."
I said, "Why?" He said, "Your liver is failing." I said, "Good, it was doing terrible work anyway."

I ran into my ex at the grocery store.
She said, "You're looking well!" I said, "Thanks, I've been really happy." She said, "Oh." I said, "Don't worry, it'll pass."

My kid asked me, "Why do people get married?"
I said, "To spend the rest of their lives with someone they love." He said, "What if they stop?" I said, "Then you learn to hide your feelings very efficiently."

I went to confession for the first time in twenty years.
The priest said, "My son, where have you been?" I said, "Honestly, doing worse things than I could confess in one sitting."

My boss asked if I had any questions about my performance review.
I said, "Yeah—how did you write this many negative things without using the word 'useless'?" He said, "I have a word limit."

I told my friend I was going on a diet.
He said, "Why?" I said, "The doctor says I need to live longer." He said, "Why would you want that?"

My mother called and asked if I was eating well.
I said, "Define 'well.'" She said, "Not pizza for dinner." I said, "Then no, I'm eating great."

I asked my barber how much longer the haircut would take.
He said, "Does it matter?" I said, "Not really, I have nowhere to be." He said, "Then why are you in such a bad mood?" I said, "Nowhere to be and nothing to do is different than you think."

My friend said he was cutting people out of his life.
I said, "That's healthy." He said, "You're next." I said, "Finally, something to look forward to."

I went to my high school reunion.
Everyone asked what I was doing now. I said, "Mostly regretting my choices." They said, "From high school?" I said, "From last week."

My dentist said, "You really need to floss more."
I said, "I'll try." He said, "Will you?" I said, "No." He said, "At least you're honest." I said, "With you? No."

I told my therapist I was feeling hopeful about the future.
She said, "That's great progress." I said, "Yeah, I figured out how to lie better."

My friend asked if I wanted to grab drinks.
I said, "Sure, when?" He said, "How about never?" I said, "That works with my schedule."

I asked my coworker if she liked working here.
She said, "It pays the bills." I said, "That's the saddest yes I've ever heard."

My mom asked why I wasn't married yet.
I said, "I'm waiting for the right person." She said, "You've been waiting ten years." I said, "Exactly. Very selective."
